newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's should spell out Names' future - agency.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's should spell out Names' future - agency.

text.p: Lloyd's of London should make clear its thinking on the future role of Names in the insurance market, members' agency LRG Cater Allen said in its latest newsletter.

Many Names, Lloyd's traditional individual backers, fear that they face extinction as corporate investors look set to account for more than 50 percent of the market next year, compared with 44 percent now.
"The present situation -- in which many Names believe there is a conspiracy theory being masterminded by some managing agents and some corporate capital -- cannot be permitted to continue," LRG said.
Lloyd's was showing a lack of leadership by saying that it had no developed policy towards the future capital base of the market, the agency added.
The number of unlimited liability Names has fallen to around 12,000 from a peak in the late 1980s of some 33,000. Many have left in the wake of the market's record losses in the early 1990s.
Lloyd's changed its rules to allow limited liability corporate investors into the market from 1994.
LRG, which as a members' agency represents the interests of Names, said the question of whether or not there was a strategy must be answered.
"Even if the answer is 'yes, but individual Names do not feature in it', at least then everyone will know where they stand," it added.
